title: Trump Issues Labor Day Proclamation Touting Manufacturing Gains, Proposes New H-1B Visa Fee
detail: President Trump proclaimed Monday, September 7, 2026, as Labor Day, issuing an official proclamation crediting American workers' 'unbreakable spirit' for six consecutive months of manufacturing expansion and record auto-plant construction, and proposing a new fee on H-1B visa petitions intended to push companies toward hiring 'qualified Americans' instead. On Truth Social, Trump paired the holiday message with an attack on the 'Radical Left Lunatics, Communists, and Dumocrats' he said were trying to 'destroy our Country,' vowing Republicans would 'win the Midterms, BIG, and SAVE AMERICA.' The dual tone — an official proclamation touting bipartisan workplace themes alongside a combative campaign-style post — came roughly two months before the November midterms.

media.caption: President Trump's Labor Day proclamation touted manufacturing gains and proposed a new H-1B visa petition fee

title: Trump Posts Second AI-Generated Image Claiming 'Hundreds of Billions' in Intel Stock Gains
detail: President Trump posted an AI-generated image to Truth Social early Monday, September 7, 2026, depicting himself day-trading Intel stock from $20 to $95 a share, captioned with a claim of making 'Hundreds of Billions of Dollars.' It was the second time Trump shared the identical image style — an earlier version last September showed Intel rising from $20 to $30, after the government took a 9.9% stake in the chipmaker. Intel shares closed at $95.80 on September 4 and touched $95.89 two days later, nearly quadrupling off a 52-week low of $24.05, but the largest documented paper gain the government holds on record is roughly $33 billion — far short of Trump's 'hundreds of billions' claim, which he did not substantiate with specific holdings or a time period. Ethics watchdogs have flagged the pattern of Trump publicly touting stocks the government holds a stake in.

media.caption: Trump's AI-generated image claiming 'hundreds of billions' in Intel stock trading gains
